- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67…), model may overfit to recent trend; apply smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting to avoid momentum traps.
